DMARC Aggregate Report Viewer

Drop the DMARC aggregate (RUA) reports from your mailbox, as .xml, .xml.gz or .zip, as many as you like. You'll see who is sending as your domain, what passes, and what would break if you moved to p=reject.

What you're looking at

Mailbox providers that support DMARC send a daily XML summary to the address in your record's rua= tag. Each record says: this IP sent N messages claiming to be from your domain, and here's how SPF, DKIM and DMARC came out. This viewer merges any number of reports, groups them by source IP and header-From domain, and shows the result for each sender.

"DMARC pass" means the message passed SPF or DKIM and that domain aligned with the visible From domain. This is the policy_evaluated result in the report. The DKIM and SPF columns show the raw authentication results, including unaligned domains. That's how you spot a third-party service signing with its own domain instead of yours.

Typical patterns

  • DKIM passes for a vendor domain, DMARC fails: a SaaS tool sends as you but signs with its own domain. Set up custom DKIM (a CNAME/TXT under your domain) in that tool.
  • DKIM passes, SPF fails, reason "forwarded": normal mail forwarding. DKIM survives forwarding and carries DMARC.
  • Everything fails from an IP you don't recognize: usually spoofing. That's exactly what p=quarantine or p=reject blocks.

FAQ

Are my DMARC reports uploaded anywhere?

No. Files are decompressed and parsed in your browser with the native DecompressionStream and DOMParser APIs. The page's Content-Security-Policy blocks requests to any third party, and the reports are never sent anywhere, not even to this site.

Which report formats are supported?

Standard RFC 7489 aggregate reports as raw XML, gzip-compressed (.xml.gz, used by Microsoft and others) or ZIP (used by Google and Yahoo). You can drop many files at once, and duplicate reports are detected by report ID and skipped.

When is it safe to move from p=none to p=reject?

Once every legitimate sending source, meaning your mail platform, CRM, ticketing, invoicing and marketing tools, passes DMARC consistently over a few weeks of reports. Moving to quarantine with a low pct= first is a common stepping stone.

Does this show forensic (RUF) reports?

No. This viewer handles aggregate (RUA) reports only. Forensic reports are individual message samples that few providers still send.
